## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement traffic mirroring for safe shadow testing, validate latency impact, and design robust rollback.

## Key Concepts
- traffic mirroring with Nginx
- docker secrets/configs
- overlay networking in Swarm
- health checks and rollback policies
- non-disruptive canary/shadow deployments

## Code Example
```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  live-api:
    image: myorg/live
    secrets: [ tls_cert, tls_key ]
  shadow-api:
    image: myorg/shadow
    secrets: [ tls_cert, tls_key ]
  edge-nginx:
    image: nginx:latest
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
    depends_on: [live-api, shadow-api]
    configs: [ api-endpoints_config ]
configs:
  api-endpoints_config:
    external: true
secrets:
  tls_cert:
    external: true
  tls_key:
    external: true
networks:
  proxy:
    driver: overlay
    attachable: true
```

```nginx
# nginx.conf (simplified)
server {
  listen 443 ssl;
  ssl_certificate /run/secrets/tls_cert;
  ssl_certificate_key /run/secrets/tls_key;
  location / {
    proxy_pass http://live-api:8080;
    mirror /mirror_shadow;
  }
  location = /mirror_shadow {
    proxy_pass http://shadow-api:8081$request_uri;
    internal;
  }
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of basic Swarm deployment, secret/config handling, and safe canary rollouts with health checks.

## Key Concepts
- Docker Secrets and Configs
- Overlay networks and Swarm deploy
- Canary rollouts and rollback on health failure
- Basic log-shipper sidecar

## Code Example
```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  api:
    image: myorg/api:latest
    secrets:
      - tls.crt
      - tls.key
    configs:
      - source: nginx_canary_conf
        target: /etc/nginx/conf.d/canary.conf
    deploy:
      replicas: 3
      update_config:
        parallelism: 1
        order: start-first
      health_check:
        test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f https://localhost/health || exit 1"]
        interval: 10s
        timeout: 5s
        retries: 3
    networks:
      - overlay_net
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    secrets:
      - tls.crt
      - tls.key
    configs:
      - source: nginx_canary_conf
        target: /etc/nginx/conf.d/canary.conf
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
      update_config:
        parallelism: 1
        order: start-first
    networks:
      - overlay_net
  log-shipper:
    image: myorg/log-shipper:latest
    volumes:
      - logs:/var/log/app
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    networks:
      - overlay_net
volumes:
  logs:
networks:
  overlay_net:
    driver: overlay
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical mTLS implementation, Docker secrets management, and edge proxy configuration in a Swarm environment. Evaluates operational skills for secure service-to-service communication.

## Key Concepts
- Docker secrets for TLS certificate management
- Nginx mutual TLS verification and client certificate validation
- Client identity propagation to backend services via HTTP headers

## Code Example
```yaml
# skeleton docker-compose.yml
version: '3.9'
services:
  edge:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - '443:443'
    secrets:
      - source: nginx_server_cert
        target: server.crt
      - source: nginx_server_key
        target: server.key
      - source: nginx_ca_cert
        target: ca.pem
    configs:
      - source: nginx_config
        target: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
  api:
    image: your-api:latest
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
secrets:
  nginx_server_cert:
    external: true
  nginx_server_key:
    external: true
  nginx_ca_cert:
    external: true
configs:
  nginx_config:
    external: true
```

## Certificate Generation
```bash
# Create private CA
openssl genrsa -out ca.key 4096
openssl req -new -x509 -days 365 -key ca.key -out ca.pem

# Generate server certificate
openssl genrsa -out server.key 2048
openssl req -new -key server.key -out server.csr
openssl x509 -req -in server.csr -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial -out server.crt -days 365

# Generate client certificate
openssl genrsa -out client.key 2048
openssl req -new -key client.key -out client.csr
openssl x509 -req -in client.csr -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial -out client.crt -days 365

# Create Docker secrets
docker secret create nginx_server_cert server.crt
docker secret create nginx_server_key server.key
docker secret create nginx_ca_cert ca.pem
```

## Testing Commands
```bash
# Test with client certificate
curl --cert client.crt --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api

# Test without client certificate (should fail)
curl --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api

# Verify client identity header
curl --cert client.crt --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api -v | grep X-Client-Subject
```

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to orchestrate multiple runtime security controls: SPIFFE-based identity management, policy enforcement via OPA, adaptive rate limiting, and observability during cross-site deployments.

Key Concepts

- SPIFFE/SVID identity issuance and validation using Vault
- Sidecar architecture for verification and policy enforcement
- Per-tenant feature gating through OPA policies
- Dynamic rate limiting with Redis-backed token buckets
- Canary deployment strategies with SLA-driven rollback mechanisms
- Multi-site Docker Swarm cluster management

Code Example

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml
version: '3.8'

services:
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
      - ./certs:/etc/nginx/certs
    depends_on:
      - api

  api:
    image: my-api:latest
    environment:
      - VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com
      - SPIFFE_WORKLOAD_API=unix:///spiffe-agent/socket
    volumes:
      - /var/run/spiffe/agent:/spiffe-agent
    depends_on:
      - redis

  verifier:
    image: spiffe-verifier:latest
    volumes:
      - /var/run/spiffe/agent:/spiffe-agent

  opa:
    image: openpolicyagent/opa:latest
    command: run --server --addr=localhost:8181 /policy
    volumes:
      - ./policy:/policy

  rate-limiter:
    image: rate-limiter:latest
    environment:
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
    depends_on:
      - redis

  redis:
    image: redis:alpine
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"

  vault:
    image: vault:latest
    environment:
      - VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com
    ports:
      - "8200:8200"
```

Bootstrap Commands:

```bash
# Initialize Docker Swarm cluster
docker swarm init --advertise-addr <MANAGER_IP>

# Join worker nodes
docker swarm join --token <TOKEN> <MANAGER_IP>:2377

# Deploy stack
docker stack deploy -c docker-compose.yml secure-api
```
